decisions.text: No WebView anywhere, in any style; nothing from a theme or the server is rendered as web content.

Three built-in styles, each a layout built into the app plus a look: Studio (the handoff layout; D28/D29 are its defaults), Play (the Companion layout from Ember: Chats / title / Shelf header, Auto's row with state captions, tool chips, the report card), HUD (the voice-first core: ring visualiser, state chip, live transcript, waveform, TYPE · HOLD TO TALK · STOP). The phone starts on Studio.

The phone's style choice defaults to 'Same as Studio' (Gerard, 24 Oct: 'install a theme in Studio and the phone changes with it' — Same as Studio is the default): the phone follows the workspace's active theme (GET /api/themes/active) until the user picks a style on the phone; picking one stores it on the phone (encrypted MMKV) and overrides; choosing 'Same as Studio' again follows the server once more. Play's and HUD's looks sync with the web through GET/PUT /api/themes/looks/automatos/play and /api/themes/looks/automatos/hud (the web HUD theme ships the phone's HUD_LOOK_SCHEMA and presets byte for byte), so a look changed in Studio repaints the phone and a look changed on the phone repaints the browser (Gerard, 24 Oct (via session PLAY): 'auto flip themes on all is very cool, when you change on web or local the mobile picks up and changes also'). Where HUD isn't installed in the workspace (404), HUD looks stay on the phone.

Studio: Light / Dark / System. Play: 'Make it yours' with six knobs (ground, accent, type, Auto's shell, Auto's light, glow), the five presets (Ember, Obsidian, Aurora, Workshop, Daylight), save, rename, delete. HUD: the Looks drawer as drawn (looks.json knobs and presets).

The Command Centre, sheets and settings are ONE set of screens dressed by each style's tokens and the shared primitives (Studio radii; Play's 6/8/10/14 radii and serif display; HUD's square panels, brackets and glyph plus WORD statuses). No screen is copied per style.

The HUD voice layout becomes the voice screen in every style in A6 (Studio ink and orange rings, Play ember with Auto in the centre, HUD its accent): this wave's RingCore, Waveform, StateChip and Transcript take their colours from the resolved style, never from HUD constants.

Fonts are the bundled TTFs (Geist, Geist Mono, Newsreader, Instrument Serif, Bricolage Grotesque, Fredoka, Rajdhani, Chakra Petch) through the foundation's FONT_FACES; an installed theme's fonts are data files it lists. Nothing is fetched from a font service at runtime.

Auto: the vendored 12-state reducer and player; HEVC-alpha .mp4 clips through expo-video on iOS; .png stills on Android and under Reduce Motion; the ring drawn by the app (Play: mint calm, the accent busy, coral for oops, dusk asleep or lost); Play's shell tint is a Skia colour matrix. Shown in Play, in HUD when the look's auto is on, and in Studio only when an installed theme brings a mascot.

Installed marketplace themes that declare a mobile block appear under Studio in the picker: the Studio layout painted with the theme's tokens, fonts and mascot from GET /api/themes/mobile/{install_id}. Themes never bring code or layouts in v1; installing stays in Studio.

The app never loads JavaScript, CSS or HTML from a theme or the server (App Store guideline 2.5.2): a theme file is downloaded only from an allowlisted /api/themes/files/ path and only as a font, a clip or a still.
Layouts read tokens only. Colour literals live only in src/styles/tokens/ (the foundation's lint rule); the vendored catalogue counts as tokens (K14).

The foundation's AiLabel is one small muted caption (Body 6, the muted token) that opens every thread in every style (the thread's first row, scrolling away) and sits on the voice screen; it is never a pill beside a composer and never disables one (no visibility fence). (D73, Gerard 23 Oct: the AI label is one small muted caption, never a pill and never a lock; the voice notice is spoken once per session) src/styles/ai-label.tsx is never edited (gate-enforced).

Nothing below 11 pt in any style (the designs' 9-10 px labels are raised to 11); Dynamic Type up to the accessibility sizes with layouts that wrap; every colour status also has a word (HUD: glyph plus WORD); every animated signal has a text twin; Reduce Motion stops loops (HUD's motion forced off, Play's rises, ring pulse and glow crossfades off) and shows stills; tap targets 44 pt.
Installed themes are listed only when the discovery document carries mobile_theme (canMobileTheme); without it the picker offers the three built-in styles.

No dependency, native module, config plugin or app.json change: package.json, package-lock.json, app.json and eas.json untouched (gate-enforced). Skia, expo-video, reanimated, gesture-handler, expo-haptics, expo-font, expo-file-system, expo-linear-gradient and react-native-svg come from the foundation's build. Bundled assets (mascot files) ship over the air.
Nothing about plans, credits or prices in any style.

No pointer to creating an account anywhere in the app, in any style: no 'Create an account', 'Sign up' or 'No account?' link, button or copy — including Play's 06 First open and every other edge screen. Apple and Google both treat a link out to sign-up as account creation, which would require in-app deletion, and the app deletes nothing (D63). Where a design shows such copy, the screen says 'Sign in with your Automatos account' or drops it. Gate-enforced on the wave's added lines.

A5 extends foundation files that no parallel kit touches (src/styles/theme.tsx, src/ui/*, app/+not-found.tsx): every change is ADDITIVE (no prop, export or type renamed or removed; useTokens() keeps its return type), so A2's and A3's code compiles unchanged when the waves meet. Every edit of a seam file (app/+not-found.tsx; in phase 2 the three shell files and every A2/A3 file) is recorded in that story's DONE notes as 'SEAM EDIT: <path> — <why>' (gate-enforced). A foundation contract that is missing or wrong: build the smallest adapter inside src/styles/ and write 'FOUNDATION GAP: <what, where>'.

Each story has a 'phase'. Phase 1 stories need only the foundation. Phase 2 stories (US-016j, US-016k, US-017g, US-016l) need A2's and A3's code in this branch (and should follow the A1 connect kit's merge, which edits the same shell files as US-016j): the gate's --print-phase prints 2 only when HEAD carries src/chat/routes.ts and src/cc/routes.ts. A build session never starts a story above the current phase; when every story of the current phase is done it finishes the phase (gate, CI commit, RALPH_COMPLETE). Phase 2 is a second launch after the base move (the launcher merges the ref that carries A2 + A3 into this branch with RALPH_BASE_MOVE=1, or the lead does it by hand).

decisions.text: Every server path this wave calls is a constant in src/styles/routes.ts (the shape scripts/check-routes.ts reads — RE-VERIFY): GET and PUT /api/themes/looks/{theme_id:path}, GET /api/themes/installed, GET /api/themes/mobile/{install_id} (pendingUpstream 'PRD-261 M-04 (#1258, merged after the pin 630fc1c85)'), GET /api/themes/files/{digest}/{path:path}. The theme id 'automatos/play' travels as two path segments, never as '%2F'. A5's own app paths live in src/styles/nav.ts (STYLE_SCREENS: settingsStyle '/settings/style', lookPlay '/settings/look/play', lookHud '/settings/look/hud') and src/navigation/routes.ts is never edited (the connect kit edits it in parallel); every other destination uses the foundation's builders.

Use the vendored modules for everything they already do and never re-implement them: lookToStudioTokens, lookToCssVars, isDarkGround, safeGlow, sheetOf, duskOf (lib/looks/engine.ts, lib/look-kit/*), tripletToHex/hexToTriplet (hsl.ts), contrastRatio/mixHex/rgba (contrast.ts, css.ts), validateLookSchema/validateLook (lib/theme-host/look-schema.ts), the Play catalogue and presets, mascotReducer, the player, ringTone/ringColour, captionFor/pageGlow, toolActivity, chatCaption, toolLineLabel. Logic from web files that are NOT vendored (editor.ts, play-look-state.ts, data-events.ts) is ported into src/styles/ with the web file named as its behaviour reference. src/core/web is never edited.

The 24 mascot files are copied byte for byte from automatos-ai frontend/public/auto/ at 630fc1c85 with git cat-file blob (binary-safe), never rewritten by an editor; .webm files (web-only) are never copied; assets/mascot/SOURCES.md records each file's source, sha256 and size. Clips are HEVC 'hvc1' 512x512, 24 fps, 5.04 s; stills 512x512 RGBA PNG (measured 20 Oct). Platform files keep the .mp4 out of the Android bundle.

Controls the designs draw with web widgets are built from what the build has: the Slider from react-native-gesture-handler + react-native-reanimated (no @react-native-community/slider); the drawer without a blur (no expo-blur); the 'Not running' command as selectable text (no expo-clipboard); gradients with expo-linear-gradient or Skia; rings, grid, scanlines and colour matrices with Skia.

HUD's looks.json (automatos-interface-look/v0) is converted to the automatos-look-schema/v1 knob shape so HUD can become a Design Kit theme later without rework: knobs ground, accent, font (choice), grid 0-30 and glow 0-40 (whole numbers), scan, auto, motion (choice 'on' | 'off', since v1 has no boolean kind); looks are automatos-interface-look/v1 documents with interface 'command'; checked with the vendored validateLookSchema / validateLook.

HUD's glow is capped exactly as Play's is: never past the vendored safeGlow for the ground and accent (text, text2, the accent text and the error text keep AA on the glow-tinted ground). With the five presets only NOVA paints one step lower (29 for 30); the slider stops at the cap.

decisions.text: The designs have no phone navigation for the Command Centre and Settings in Play and HUD, so: Play's Conversations and Shelf screens get a bottom bar 'Chats · Shelf · Centre' (Centre = the Command Centre with the server's needs-you number) and an avatar chip to Settings; Play's chat shows a slim 'NEEDS YOU · N  Command Centre →' line under its header when the server's total is above zero (FR-4); HUD's core gets a command row under its top bar: 'COMMAND · N', 'LOOK' (the desktop top bar's LOOK button), and a menu square to Settings. Settings → 'Style and look' is the picker in every style (the Settings row lands in phase 2, US-016j, because the settings index is shared with the connect kit; in phase 1 the picker is reached by its route).

Untinted clips (Play's Bronze shell, HUD, a theme's mascot) play through expo-video's VideoView. A tinted shell (Gold, Silver, Cobalt) has to be drawn through a Skia ColorMatrix, which cannot filter a native video view: it plays the same .mp4 through Skia's useVideo when MASCOT_TINTED_CLIPS is true (default), else shows the tinted still. If the device check finds a black box (alpha lost), the owner flips the one constant over the air.
HUD corner brackets: 14 x 1.5 pt L-shapes at all four corners in the accent at 0.7 alpha, as 'Automatos Command HUD.dc.html' draws them (its README says top-left and bottom-right; the drawing wins).
Play's First open keeps Ember's three starter chips; a tap fills the composer and never sends. D29's no-chips rule is the Studio composer's default (D56); Studio's First open shows none.

userStories.notes: Server: orchestrator/api/themes_looks.py (gate members:read; per workspace and per user; a theme not installed → 404) and services/themes/looks.py. RE-VERIFY after foundation: how scripts/check-routes.ts normalises '{theme_id:path}' and how src/api/client.ts substitutes a path parameter — if it encodes the whole value, build a feature-local substitution that encodes each segment and write FOUNDATION GAP. The phone sees the look last saved on the server, not one still being edited in a browser tab (docs/theme-host/mobile.md). 24 Oct: HUD joins the sync (Gerard via PLAY); the web theme automatos/hud ships HUD_LOOK_SCHEMA exactly. | US-017d DONE 24 Oct (3f6e7a2, 301178c, 911a3fb): play/{looks-api,looks-schemas,look-sync,look-store,play-looks}.ts, sync/{look-outbox,look-marks,look-themes,look-sync-run,foreground}.ts, sync/LookSync.tsx in StyleSync; Play's and HUD's looks share one engine, one runner per theme, one outbox. FOUNDATION GAP: src/api/url.ts fillPath fills only '{name}' and encodes the whole value, so play/looks-api.ts looksRoute fills '{theme_id:path}' segment by segment. Security (the security hook's two findings, fixed): the phone's one copy belongs to an owner '<server>|<workspace>|<user>' (useAuthSession().ownerId) kept in styles.*.looks.sync; LookSync claims before anything is read, merged or sent; another owner's copy, or a non-blank copy whose owner cannot be read, starts from the theme's defaults (fail closed); a save queued for an owner the phone no longer has is never sent. Beyond the AC: 400/409/413/422 drop the marks (the web's refused statuses less 403/404); a phone change before the first meeting is only marked (a PUT then would replace the server's looks unmerged); a read that saw a save queued meanwhile is dropped. defaultLook is string | null (looks.py answers null). No SEAM EDIT (src/styles/** only; provider/store.ts additive: playLooks, setPlayLooks, lookSync, setLookSync; StyleSources.playLook became playLooks, A5's own type). For later stories: US-017e / US-018c edit through useStyleStore setPlayLooks / setPlayLook / setHudLooks (the runner sees the change and sends it) and read useLookSyncNotice('play' | 'hud') (LOOK_SYNC_COPY.localOnly is the 'Kept on this phone only' line); freshPlayLookId and checkPlayLook are in play/play-looks.ts. US-016j: StyleSync in the shell; on sign-out the looks stay on the phone under their owner (the next owner's claim resets them), so no clearing is needed for privacy. Gate note: 'HUD looks never reach the server (D59)' predates the 24 Oct HUD sync decision; it passes because the sync lives in src/styles/play and src/styles/sync, not src/styles/hud. D-TOKENS still fails only on the earlier stories' rgba() helper calls, none in this story's lines.

userStories.title: Look sync: a read that overlaps a save never puts the phone back on the server's older look
userStories.description: Review finding (MEDIUM, US-017d / D-PHONE-CHOICE: 'overwrites a phone change with an older server read'). src/styles/sync/look-sync-run.ts:127-134 readAndApply drops a read only when rt.sends changed while it ran (a save QUEUED during the read). A save already in flight when the read starts (queued before it, so counted in sendsBefore), or one the outbox only dispatches during the read (src/styles/sync/look-outbox.ts:29-30, tail.then(run)), is not seen. Interleaving: a knob change → queueSend (sends 1, PUT A in flight) → the look page opens or the app returns to the foreground → refresh → GET starts (sendsBefore 1) and the server serves it before PUT A commits → PUT A answers → 'kept' clears lookChanged (look-sync.ts:202-205) → the GET answers with the pre-PUT copy, rt.sends is still 1 so it is applied → serverTruth (look-sync.ts:159-164) takes the server's older active look; settle (look-sync.ts:176) then finds nothing changed, so nothing is re-sent. The phone shows the old look while the server holds the new one until the next foreground read, and an edit made meanwhile is made on top of the old look. The file's own header (look-sync-run.ts:11-12) promises 'an answer ... read while a save was sent, is dropped'. The web reads once per scope (play-look-store.ts @ 630fc1c85 'Once per scope and theme'), so it never had this overlap; the phone's foreground reads add it.
acceptanceCriteria: Cause: readAndApply's guard (look-sync-run.ts:132) counts saves queued during the read but not a save in flight or answered during it → DONE — 0b849f5: readAndApply's guard only compared rt.sends before/after the read; a save in flight at the read's start (counted in sendsBefore) or answered during it was not seen (reproduced: the new overlap test fails on HEAD~1's runner, the phone went back to DEFAULT_LOOK)

Change: a read is applied only when no save of that theme was queued, in flight or answered at any point between the read's start and its answer (e.g. the runtime counts answered saves beside rt.sends and drops the answer unless both are unchanged AND nothing was outstanding when the read started); a dropped read changes nothing on the phone and the next mount / foreground / look-page open reads again (no timer, no retry loop, no polling); the header comment says exactly what is dropped → DONE — 0b849f5: look-outbox queue() now returns a promise settling when the save's turn is over (answered, failed or dropped for a newer one); the runtime counts answered beside sends (after the answer's dispatch); noSaveSince() applies a read's answer or failure only when sends === answered at its start and neither moved since; a dropped read writes nothing; no timer/retry/polling; header lines 10-15 say exactly what is dropped

Test (src/styles/sync/__tests__/look-sync-run.test.ts, a fake client whose GET and PUT promises the test resolves by hand): (1) PUT in flight → GET starts → PUT answers → GET answers with the pre-PUT copy → the store's active look is still the phone's newer one and no second PUT is sent; (2) the same with the GET answering BEFORE the PUT keeps today's behaviour (the phone's look kept, sent again only if the server lacks it); (3) a read with no save outstanding is applied as today; every existing test in the file still passes → DONE — 0b849f5: look-sync-run.test.ts 'a read that overlaps a save' (handServer: GET/PUT answered by hand): (1) PUT answers before the pre-PUT GET → playLook OBSIDIAN, 1 PUT; (2) GET answers first → phone's look kept, PUT lands, nothing sent again (1 PUT), and when that PUT fails the next read sends it again (2 PUTs); (3) a read with no save outstanding is applied (AURORA); plus a save the outbox replaced still lets the next read apply (EMBER); all 10 earlier tests still pass (15/15)
